2. View: The view is responsible for displaying the user interface of the application to the user. It listens to changes made by the controller and updates itself accordingly to reflect any changes in the model's state.

3. Controller: The controller acts as an intermediary between the model and the view, handling user interactions and updating both the model and view accordingly. It also manages navigation between views when necessary.

Here's a simple diagram of the MVC architecture:

```
User Interaction --> Controller
                    |
                    |---> Model (Data & Business Logic)
                    |
                    |<--- View (UI)
```

In this setup, when a user interacts with the application, the event is handled by the controller. The controller then modifies the model's data if needed and triggers the view to update its display accordingly, reflecting the changes in the model. This separation of concerns allows developers to work on each component independently while ensuring that they all function together seamlessly.
